서서히 녹는 약은 소장을 충분히 오래 지나가야 약이 나와요. 장이 짧거나 빨리 지나가면 약의 일부가 나오기 전에 몸 밖으로 나갈 수 있어요.
서서히 녹는 약은 약의 일부를 대장에서 내보내기도 해요. 대장이 없으면 약이 나올 시간과 공간이 줄어들어요.
장루가 있는 분에게 서방정은 잘 녹지 않을 위험이 큰 제형으로 분류돼요. 물약과 빨리 녹는 일반 정제는 위험이 낮은 쪽으로 분류돼요.
먹는 약이 얼마나 잘 흡수되는지는 장루 종류보다 남은 소장의 길이와 상태에 더 많이 좌우돼요.
라벨에는 디클로페낙이 먹었을 때 다 흡수된다고 적혀 있어요. 하지만 라벨의 약동학 항목은 빠져 있어서, 서방정이 장 어디에서 녹는지는 라벨에서 확인할 수 없었어요.
한 연구에서 장루가 있는 50명 중 11명이 녹지 않은 약을 본 적이 있었어요. 60% 넘는 사람은 장루가 약에 어떤 영향을 주는지 들은 적이 없다고 했어요.

final.verdict: 약을 끊을지, 속방형으로 바꿀지는 약사나 처방한 의사가 정할 일이에요. 파우치에 보인 알약은 약이 녹지 않았다는 뜻일 수도 있고, 약이 다 나온 뒤 남은 빈 껍데기일 수도 있으니 약사에게 보여 줄 만해요.

why.claim: 파우치에 알약이나 껍데기가 그대로 보이면 약이 녹지 않았다는 뜻일 수도 있고, 약이 나온 뒤 남은 빈 껍데기일 수도 있어요. 약사에게 보여 줄 만하지만, 어느 쪽인지 증거는 아니에요.
이 제품의 제형은 '서방정(TABLET, EXTENDED RELEASE)'이에요.
서서히 녹는 약은 소장을 충분히 오래 지나가야 약이 나와요. 장이 짧거나 빨리 지나가면 약의 일부가 나오기 전에 몸 밖으로 나갈 수 있어요.
서서히 녹는 약은 약의 일부를 대장에서 내보내기도 해요. 대장이 없으면 약이 나올 시간과 공간이 줄어들어요.
장루가 있는 분에게 서방정은 잘 녹지 않을 위험이 큰 제형으로 분류돼요. 물약과 빨리 녹는 일반 정제는 위험이 낮은 쪽으로 분류돼요.
라벨에는 디클로페낙이 먹었을 때 다 흡수된다고 적혀 있어요. 하지만 라벨의 약동학 항목은 빠져 있어서, 서방정이 장 어디에서 녹는지는 라벨에서 확인할 수 없었어요.
한 연구에서 장루가 있는 50명 중 11명이 녹지 않은 약을 본 적이 있었어요. 60% 넘는 사람은 장루가 약에 어떤 영향을 주는지 들은 적이 없다고 했어요.

draft.verdict: Whether to stop Inderal XL or switch to the immediate-release kind is a decision for your prescriber or pharmacist, not one to make alone; the guidelines do flag extended-release capsules like this one as a real concern with your anatomy, and the beads you saw are worth showing your pharmacist.

why.claim: Inderal XL is an extended-release capsule.
Time-release medicines need enough time in the small bowel to let out their drug. When the bowel is shorter or moves fast, part of the dose may leave the body before it is released.
Slow-release products may release part of their dose in the large intestine. Your colon is not connected, so these products have less time and less surface to release the drug.
After a large small-bowel resection, guidelines say sustained-release medicines are generally avoided, because they rely on a long, normal transit.
Beads or a shell in the pouch can mean the medicine did not dissolve. They can also be empty shells left after the drug came out. It is worth showing the pharmacist, but it is not proof either way.
How well pills are absorbed depends more on how long and healthy the remaining small bowel is than on the type of stoma.
Crushing or opening extended-release products defeats their design and can be dangerous.
Even when the drug is absorbed well, the liver breaks down much of it, so on average only about a quarter of propranolol reaches the bloodstream.

draft.verdict: I can't stand in for your pharmacist or tell you what to do with your metformin, but here is what the label and guidelines say, plus one question to take to your real pharmacist.

why.claim: This product is a liquid, not a tablet.
Liquid forms may be absorbed more reliably than solid tablets in short bowel syndrome.
Most medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel, the first part of the jejunum. Many plain immediate-release medicines can still be absorbed when that part remains.
How well medicines are absorbed depends more on how long and healthy your remaining small bowel is than on the type of stoma.
Liquid medicines often contain sugar alcohols like sorbitol. These pull water into the gut and can raise stoma output.

The part of the label we found lists benzoic acid, hydrochloric acid and potassium bicarbonate as inactive ingredients. The full inactive-ingredient section was missing, so we couldn't check the whole list.
The label says the body took up more of the medicine when it was taken with a meal than on an empty stomach.
If a medicine may not be absorbed well after bowel surgery, your care team can look at other forms of the same drug.

draft.verdict: I can't act as your doctor, even hypothetically, because what to do with Revatio is your prescriber's decision. What I can tell you is that I found nothing in the sources I checked that flags this plain tablet for a small bowel joined to the colon, though how well it absorbs depends on how much small bowel you have, and that isn't known.

why.claim: The label lists Revatio as a plain immediate-release tablet. It is not a timed-release or coated-release design.
The guidelines say timed-release and coated tablets are generally avoided after a large bowel resection. That warning is about those designs, not plain tablets like this one.
Most medicines you swallow are absorbed in the upper small bowel. Many plain immediate-release medicines can still be absorbed if that part is still there.
The label says sildenafil is absorbed quickly by mouth. On average about 41% reaches the blood, anywhere from 25% to 63%.
How well medicines are absorbed depends mostly on how long and healthy the rest of your small bowel is. Your length isn't known.
In studies of people who had bowel surgery, 29 of 37 drugs were absorbed less well. The effect was different for each drug, so nobody can predict it for one person from the studies alone.
The label's ingredient list shows microcrystalline cellulose and silicon dioxide, with no sorbitol listed. The separate inactive-ingredient section was missing, so this list may not be complete.

why.claim: Dimetane అనే పేరుతో ఉన్న ఒక లేబుల్ దొరికింది. అది లిక్విడ్ నింపిన క్యాప్సూల్. కానీ అది మీ దగ్గర ఉన్న మందుదేనని నేను ఖచ్చితంగా చెప్పలేను.
ఆ లేబుల్ లోపలి పదార్థాల జాబితాలో సార్బిటాల్ ఉంది.
సార్బిటాల్ లాంటి షుగర్ ఆల్కహాల్స్ సరిగ్గా శోషించబడవు, పేగులోకి నీటిని లాగుతాయి. దాంతో స్టోమా అవుట్‌పుట్ పెరగవచ్చు.
నోటి ద్వారా వేసుకునే చాలా మందులు చిన్న పేగు పై భాగంలో (జెజునమ్ మొదటి భాగంలో) శోషించబడతాయి. ఆ భాగం మిగిలి ఉంటే, చాలా సాధారణ (immediate-release) మందులు ఇంకా శోషించబడవచ్చు.

final.verdict: ఊహాత్మకంగా అయినా, మీ ఫార్మసిస్ట్ లేదా డాక్టర్ లాగా Dimetane క్యాప్సూల్‌తో మీరు ఏమి చేయాలో నేను చెప్పలేను, ఎందుకంటే అది మీ ఫార్మసిస్ట్ లేదా డాక్టర్ తీసుకోవాల్సిన నిర్ణయం. నాకు దొరికిన లేబుల్ మీ క్యాప్సూల్‌దేనని కూడా నేను నిర్ధారించలేకపోయాను, కాబట్టి ప్యాకెట్‌పై ఉన్న ఖచ్చితమైన స్పెల్లింగ్ చూసి పంపండి, లేదా లేబుల్ స్పష్టంగా కనిపించే ఫోటో పంపండి.

why.claim: Dimetane అనే పేరుతో ఉన్న ఒక లేబుల్ దొరికింది. అది లిక్విడ్ నింపిన క్యాప్సూల్. కానీ అది మీ దగ్గర ఉన్న మందుదేనని నేను ఖచ్చితంగా చెప్పలేను.
ఆ లేబుల్ లోపలి పదార్థాల జాబితాలో సార్బిటాల్ ఉంది.
సార్బిటాల్ లాంటి షుగర్ ఆల్కహాల్స్ సరిగ్గా శోషించబడవు, పేగులోకి నీటిని లాగుతాయి. దాంతో స్టోమా అవుట్‌పుట్ పెరగవచ్చు.
నోటి ద్వారా వేసుకునే చాలా మందులు చిన్న పేగు పై భాగంలో (జెజునమ్ మొదటి భాగంలో) శోషించబడతాయి. ఆ భాగం మిగిలి ఉంటే, చాలా సాధారణ (immediate-release) మందులు ఇంకా శోషించబడవచ్చు.
మందు ఎంత బాగా శోషించబడుతుందనేది, స్టోమా రకం కంటే మిగిలిన చిన్న పేగు పొడవు, దాని ఆరోగ్యం మీదే ఎక్కువగా ఆధారపడి ఉంటుంది.
మందు సరిగ్గా శోషించబడకపోవచ్చు అనిపిస్తే, అదే మందు యొక్క వేరే రూపాల (ద్రవం, కరిగే రూపం, చర్మంపై పూసేది, లేదా నోటి ద్వారా కాని రూపం) గురించి కేర్ టీమ్ ఆలోచించవచ్చు.

evidence.G:aga-sbs#fluids-ors: A glucose-electrolyte oral rehydration solution (ORS) is the preferred drink to replace fluid and sodium losses in short bowel syndrome, especially with a jejunostomy.

why.claim: The label lists this product as an extended-release tablet.

draft.verdict: I can't give a yes or no, because that's a decision for your pharmacist or prescriber; Zestril is a plain, uncoated, immediate-release tablet, which is the kind many bodies with short bowel can still absorb, but it contains mannitol, a sugar alcohol that can raise output.

why.claim: Zestril is a white, round, uncoated, immediate-release tablet.
Most oral medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel, so many plain immediate-release drugs can still be absorbed when that part remains.
How well a medicine is absorbed depends more on the length and health of the remaining small bowel. Your small-bowel length isn't known, so it's hard to judge this for your body.
The guideline concern about timed-release and coated designs applies to sustained-release and delayed-release medicines. Zestril is neither.
The label lists mannitol as an inactive ingredient in the tablets.
Mannitol and other sugar alcohols are poorly absorbed. They draw water into the gut and can raise stoma output or diarrhea.
The label says food does not change how much Zestril the body takes in.
Thirst, dark or reduced urine, dizziness on standing and rising output are warning signs of dehydration. Raise them with your care team promptly.

evidence.G:aga-sbs#dehydration-signs: Thirst, dark or reduced urine, dizziness on standing, and rising stoma output are warning signs of dehydration that should be raised with the care team promptly.
evidence.G:aga-sbs#diet-simple-sugars: Concentrated simple sugars (sweets, syrups, sweetened drinks) draw water into the bowel and are generally limited in short bowel syndrome.
evidence.G:aga-sbs#fluids-hypertonic: Hypertonic, sugary drinks such as fruit juice and regular soda pull water into the gut and can raise stoma output or diarrhea in short bowel syndrome; they are best limited regardless of anatomy.
evidence.G:aga-sbs#fluids-ors: A glucose-electrolyte oral rehydration solution (ORS) is the preferred drink to replace fluid and sodium losses in short bowel syndrome, especially with a jejunostomy.
evidence.G:aga-sbs#medications-proximal-absorptio: Most oral medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel (the first part of the jejunum), so many plain immediate-release drugs can still be absorbed when that segment remains.
evidence.G:aga-sbs#medications-release-forms: After extensive small-bowel resection, sustained-release and delayed-release (including enteric-coated) medicines are generally avoided because they depend on a long, normal transit to release the drug.
evidence.G:pd-2017#ors-sodium: For short bowel syndrome, oral rehydration solutions with a sodium concentration of about 90 to 120 mmol/L are generally recommended; this is higher than many commercial rehydration drinks.
evidence.G:pd-2017#salt: Salting food and choosing salty snacks is commonly encouraged in short bowel syndrome with high output, within the care team's advice for the person's heart and kidney health.
evidence.G:pd-2017#sports-drinks: Typical sports drinks are low in sodium and high in sugar compared with an SBS oral rehydration solution, so they are not a substitute for it.
evidence.G:pg139#enteric-coating: Enteric-coated and delayed-release products are designed to pass the stomach before dissolving; with rapid transit, the coating may not dissolve in time, and some pass through intact.
evidence.G:pg139#liquid-forms: Liquid forms may be absorbed more reliably than solid tablets in short bowel syndrome, but liquid medicines often contain sugar alcohols that can increase output.
evidence.G:pg139#sugar-alcohols: Sorbitol, xylitol, mannitol and other sugar alcohols are poorly absorbed, draw water into the gut, and can raise stoma output or diarrhea; they are common inactive ingredients in liquid medicines and sugar-free products.
evidence.G:pg139#time-release: Time-release formulations depend on adequate small-bowel transit time to release their drug; with a shortened bowel or rapid transit, part of the dose may leave the body before it is released.
evidence.G:sood-2013#residual-length: How well oral medicines are absorbed tracks the length and health of the remaining small bowel more than the type of stoma.
evidence.G:who-ors#purpose: Oral rehydration solution works because glucose and sodium are absorbed together in the small bowel, carrying water with them.
evidence.G:who-ors#reduced-osmolarity-composition: WHO reduced-osmolarity ORS (2003) contains sodium 75 mmol/L, chloride 65, glucose 75, potassium 20 and citrate 10 mmol/L (total 245 mOsm/L). It was designed for acute diarrhea, and its sodium is below the range usually cited for short bowel syndrome.
